claims.source: Los Alamos National Laboratory, 'The Los Alamos Primer', National Security Science https://www.lanl.gov/media/publications/national-security-science/0723-the-los-alamos-primer
claims.text: Los Alamos National Laboratory's own account of the Los Alamos Primer states: 'Physicist Edward Condon transcribed the lectures and compiled the notes into the first official Los Alamos technical report, or LA-1.' The lectures were Robert Serber's, given in April 1943, and LA-1 was declassified in 1965. Three American Alchemy episodes describe Condon as having written the Primer; the laboratory's account gives him the transcribing and compiling role and gives the lectures to Serber.

claims.source: Lt Col Robert R. Hippler to Dr Edward U. Condon, 16 January 1967, Headquarters United States Air Force, pages 1 and 2, https://www.nicap.org/docs/HipplerLetters.pdf
claims.text: Lt Col Robert R. Hippler of the Science Division, Directorate of Science and Technology, Headquarters USAF, wrote to Condon on 16 January 1967: 'When you have looked into some sightings and examined some Blue Book records and become acquainted with the true state of affairs, you must consider the cost of the Air Force program on UFOs, and determine if the taxpayer should support this for the next decade.' The letter calls itself informal, says it expresses Hippler's own opinion and 'is not binding on you', and names its second subject as 'an apparently obscure understanding of what the Air Force wants'. Two Michels speakers describe this memo from memory without producing it; this is the document.

claims.source: 'Scientific Study of Unidentified Flying Objects', University of Colorado, 1968, title page and letter of transmittal
claims.text: The report was produced under US Air Force contract 44620-67-C-0035 with the University of Colorado, with Condon as scientific director.

claims.source: USAF Fact Sheet, 'Unidentified Flying Objects and Air Force Project Blue Book'
claims.text: The Air Force cited the Colorado study, a National Academy of Sciences review and prior Air Force experience as the basis for terminating Blue Book on 17 December 1969.

The Condon Report itself documents the 1948 Estimate of the Situation, its rejection by Vandenberg and the destruction of copies — a disclosure buried in Section V Chapter 2 while the conclusions at the front declared the subject unworthy of study.

label: Edward U. Condon
narrative: Edward Condon was a distinguished quantum physicist, former director of the National Bureau of Standards, and a man who had himself been hounded by the House Un-American Activities Committee — which made him an unusually credentialled front for the Air Force's exit strategy. Under contract 44620-67-C-0035, awarded October 1966, he directed the University of Colorado UFO Project and personally wrote the summary, conclusions and recommendations that were placed at the front of the 1968 report and were the only part most readers ever saw. Those conclusions declared further study unwarranted. The body of the report did not support them: roughly a third of the cases studied were left unexplained by the project's own investigators. Condon spent much of the project period giving speeches disparaging the subject, told an audience in January 1967 that the study was 'a bunch of nonsense' and that he might recommend the government get out of it, and fired the two staff members who exposed the Low memo. His report was blessed by a National Academy of Sciences panel and used by the Air Force as the stated basis for terminating Blue Book on 17 December 1969. Condon delivered exactly what the Robertson Panel had prescribed fifteen years earlier, with academic letterhead attached.
